content:
mike_s: Heads-up — ACME legal wants to validate an on-prem, air-gapped POC. They asked if we can do a hybrid flow: local inference nodes fully offline with a periodic signed bundle sync pushed by their ops team or pulled behind a bastion. Need a short presales writeup I can send that covers packaging, delta updates, signing/verification, license activation, expected bundle sizes, and any legal/compliance blockers. Can we assemble bullet answers here?

jana_se: Yes, doable. For POC we usually recommend a push-style signed bundle (they don't open inbound ports). For medium term, prefer pull-through-bastion to schedule maintenance windows. Key Qs to ask ACME before kickoff: 1) node count and CPU/GPU types, 2) allowed OS images and package managers, 3) EDR/MDM policies, 4) whether a scheduled outbound HTTPS window is allowed.

liam_eng: Packaging notes:
- Artifact: gzipped tarball with installer binary, manifest.json, sbom.spdx, model files, and a signature file.
- Manifest includes checksums (sha256) and a version field.
- Signing: we sign bundles with PKCS#7 by default; can also emit detached sig and provide our public cert. Customer can supply their public key to verify.
- Typical sizes: small quantized runtime + small model ~250-500MB; mid-range model ~2-4GB; multi-model packs 6-10GB. For POC assume 1 full bundle transfer.
- Deltas: we provide binary deltas for model weights and small patch bundles for runtime/security fixes (usually 5-60MB). Deltas are rsync-friendly and reduce transfer sizes.

liam_eng: Offline apply example (to include in the note):
```
# verify signature
redwood-install verify --bundle /tmp/acme-bundle.tar.gz --sig /tmp/acme-bundle.sig --pubkey /etc/redwood/pub.pem
# apply bundle
sudo redwood-install apply /tmp/acme-bundle.tar.gz --offline --accept-license
```
We enforce signature verification by default; we can add a hook to call out to a pkcs11 module if they want to integrate an HSM for verification.

emily_sec: Security/compliance items to flag to ACME:
- SBOM: SPDX supplied with each bundle, plus a vuln-scan summary. Recommend they run their SBOM scanner.
- Certs/Keys: We can store signing keys in our KMS or accept their public key. For enterprise installs, recommend customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Audit logs: nodes keep locally signed audit records; these can be exported to customer SIEM on next-available connectivity.
- Telemetry: no inference telemetry leaves the node unless they enable it. We can produce a data-flow diagram for SOC2/legal review.
- FIPS: we have a FIPS-compatible crypto mode; confirm if required.
- Patch SLA: propose 48-72h for critical CVEs (contract clause).

jana_se: Licensing & pricing quick bullets for the note:
- POC (up to 90 days): no packaging charge; limited business-hours SRE support.
- Private/offline deployment: one-time packaging fee + annual maintenance/license per node band.
- Activation: file-based license tied to org ID and node count. Time-bound license tokens available for POC to avoid outbound checks.
- If they want automated pulls or integration work, include Professional Services hours on quote.

deploy-bot: POC runbook uploaded: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc/offline-hybrid-sync-v1 (internal link) :package:

mike_s: This is great. Two follow-ups: upgrade cadence recommendations for minimal disruption, and any enterprise blockers that usually come from legal/security teams?

liam_eng: Recommended rollout cadence:
1) POC: push-mode, manual apply, smoke tests. No auto-update.
2) Pilot: enable delta updates via scheduled pull behind bastion; metadata sync nightly; full model sync weekly or as needed.
3) Prod: scheduled monthly full bundles, security hotfixes/patch bundles as needed (critical patches within 48-72h). We support canary tags so they can apply to subset first.
We avoid forced automatic updates unless customer explicitly opts in.

emily_sec: Common enterprise blockers to call out so ACME can pre-empt:
- Requirement for FIPS-validated crypto or specific cipher suites.
- Requirement to review SBOM or third-party licenses before approval.
- Requirement to host signing keys in their HSM/KMS (we support this).
- Legal wanting a data-flow diagram and assurance that telemetry is opt-in.
- Need for a defined patch SLA in contract for critical vulnerabilities.

mike_s: Perfect, I'll package this into a one-pager and ask for the node list, OS images, EDR/MDM policy, and whether they can provide a bastion or maintenance window. Also will send the data-flow diagram and the internal runbook link. Schedule kickoff tentatively for next Wed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
